I looked up the spec sheet on the 555 DIS is open collector which sort of changes what will need to be done. I think the problem with the first circuit is the original r1 value was so high the gate voltage ended up being very low when pin 7 closes and the gate on the mosfet goes high in phase with pin 3 which is output. You were getting the ringing and low light output from that thats why using a 100 ohm resistor in place of the 10k worked better as the gate voltage would be higher with a lower resistance. I think you should be using pin 3 to drive the mosfet. Pin 3 will output voltage around 1.7v below the 12 volts you are supplying the 555 with. Also using pin 3 will be more power efficient because you soak a bunch of power through r1 when pin 7 goes open drain thats why you had to change to a 1/4 watt resistor.

Check out this for a couple of alternate wiring's for driving a mosfet with the 555 from pin 3

I'm favoring the second schematic using the push-pull (totem pole) driver configuration as that will give you the full 12v on the mosfet gate you really want the gate voltage to be as high as possible to ensure the mosfet can open fully quickly when it goes high.

Also check out the wiki article on the 555 particularly the astable section as it has the formulas for determining the frequency using the pin 7 open drain, a couple of resistors which could be replaced by a pot and a capacitor.
